page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with 5669 GB of NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

The processor architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which accelerate vector and matrix operations. In performance benchmarks, the server demonstrates top-tier capabilities, particularly in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, passmark CPU extended instructions, and passmark CPU encryption tests. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks reaches top-tier levels at 7496.51 GB/sec, while large block read and write operations maintain strong performance.

The hardware profile translates to high throughput in database and memory-intensive workloads. Redis SET operations achieve top-tier performance at 159.97 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is recorded at 143.95 GB/sec. Additionally, the server exhibits strong performance in LLM inference prompt processing for both small and medium models. This resource density and high-speed local NVMe storage make the E96ds_v7 highly cost-efficient for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers, and data-intensive enterprise workloads without requiring dedicated GPU acceleration.
